tools_used: file reads of the blinded staging area, event.yaml, outcome.json, record/context.json, the stored snapshot, documents.json
grep over record/documents/application.txt to check a candidate's factual assertions
helpful: The staged retrieval_log.json with result_capture markers: the 0.0 coverage on one candidate made it immediately clear the calls had to be graded on their queries.
The stored snapshot's ProceedingsandOrder list settled the disposition shape (single-Justice denial, no referral) in one read.
The interim-stage rule in the prompt that the baseline is the harness's removed a whole class of hand-pooling decisions.
gaps: The predictor's big_case_score sits in the same prediction.json as everything else a grade needs, so the 'form your read before seeing theirs' instruction is hard to honour in practice; staging that field apart (or last) would make the independence real.

A candidate's own flags.json is not staged (by design), but where it reports a data-quality problem that the evaluator's view contradicts, there is no structured way to link the two; a flag naming the alias is the workaround.
notes: Interim cell, two forward candidates, both correct on the label. No corpus queries were needed: the provisioned record and the statpack section carried everything the grading required.
